author: fashion_forum_user_1
text: My Myntra wishlist is overloaded now. I save heels and sneakers there, but when I come back later I cannot remember which ones were actually worth buying.

author: fashion_forum_user_2
text: I treat wishlist like a moodboard for dresses. I hold off until I know the occasion and can see enough real customer photos to trust the look.

author: fashion_forum_user_3
text: For saved shoes I still leave Myntra to look for fit reviews and styling tips, because the app alone does not remove my doubt.

author: fashion_forum_user_4
text: I save festive outfits in wishlist and wait until I confirm the event mood, so many products sit there for weeks.

author: fashion_forum_user_5
text: My wishlist is basically a bookmark list for outfits I might buy later, but later often never comes because I lose context.

author: fashion_forum_user_6
text: Saved shoes on Myntra need better fit cues. Without them, I end up researching elsewhere and forgetting to come back.

author: fashion_forum_user_7
text: Once my wishlist crosses twenty products, it stops helping me choose and starts making every decision harder.

author: fashion_forum_user_8
text: I save dresses and tops, but I need styling proof from influencers or real users before I convert those saved items.

author: fashion_forum_user_9
text: Most of my saved ethnic wear is tied to potential events, so if plans change those wishlist items never get bought.

author: fashion_forum_user_10
text: I shortlist products on Myntra but still compare them against AJIO and other apps, and that slows me down a lot.
